T845 — dispatch must honour the caps (untracked/T845-dispatch-honours-caps.md). The caps existed; the door most work goes through did not read them. Landmark: advances L1 (dispatch tooling) — one door, one set of limits.

== THE DEFECT ==
tools/fleet-keeper.sh read FLEET_CAP (default 5) and FLEET_FAMILY_CAP ("family=N", default claude=3,fable=1 — T651 §7c.33) and refused over them; bin/dispatch contained ZERO references to either (measured: grep -c → 0). While the keeper sat refusing at 1, twelve workers ran (7 ollama + 5 deepseek), all dispatched explicitly — the "two doors, one gated" defect in its fourth instance (nonce+meter; close-path; appetite; now caps).

== WHAT WAS BUILT ==
1. tools/fleet_caps.py (NEW, the shared helper): the family map (canonical label → family), the defaults, the counters (in_progress total, per-family, held-file set) and the override ledger. bin/dispatch AND the keeper's embedded Python both import it — ONE counter, ONE definition (brief §2: "count the same thing the same way, from the same helper, so the two doors cannot disagree about how full the fleet is"). The keeper's own log lines and loop behaviour are unchanged; only the source of the numbers moved. Verified byte-identical log lines via the regression: 'at cap (2/2) — no dispatch' and 'family-cap: T8711 family claude at cap 1/1' are pinned.
2. bin/dispatch — the fleet-cap gate, after the provider-window gate: refuses over the TOTAL cap (FLEET_CAP) and the FAMILY cap (FLEET_FAMILY_CAP), the refusal naming the cap, the current count, and the waiting tasks (the brief's exact requirement); then the one-writer holds check (brief §5: a dispatch whose holds intersect a RUNNING task's holds is refused, naming the file and the holder — "make the door notice"); then --override-cap=<reason> (brief §3): bypasses the caps for THIS dispatch only, reason REQUIRED and appended to untracked/fleet-cap-overrides.jsonl exactly the way the T677 window override appends to fleet-window-overrides.jsonl; a dry-run override is reported but NOT recorded (a dry-run is not a decision — T677 precedent); the override NEVER bypasses the one-writer check (D022's 'dispatch-anyway after a wait' escape was REJECTED by the operator on 2026-08-20 and is gone from the keeper; the door gets no softer doctrine). All gates read the SAME kanban snapshot (fetched once via fleet_caps.read_rows — the row-state gate, the T628 probe gate and the caps gate can no longer disagree with each other; the old row_state subprocess fetch and the probe gate's second fetch are gone, one subprocess saved per dispatch).
3. tools/fleet-keeper.sh — replaced its inline FAMILY map / DEFAULT_FAMILY_CAP / family_of / family_cap / family_inprog / inprog_holds with the shared helper (thin local wrappers so the log lines keep their exact format).

== THE DEFAULTS PROPOSAL (brief §4 — each number defended with evidence, not taste) ==
FLEET_CAP = 4 (total). The 2026-08-19 ruling committed 5 as the KEEPER's cap; the 2026-08-24 operator ruling asks to "run more sequentially/serially even if tasks CAN run in parallel conflict-free", and the explicit door now enforces the same number, so the effective fleet is bounded by both doors. Derivation: 4 = the claude family cap (3) + 1 — the only family with a provider ceiling below 5 — so even a full claude race leaves exactly one lane for other families, while 3 would starve non-claude work whenever a race runs. Evidence anchors: the 12-worker incident (7 ollama + 5 deepseek, all over any cap); DeepSeek's uncapped 513 M input tokens in one day — the total is the ONLY bound on the uncapped families; ollama's five-worker ceiling becomes unreachable-by-accident.
FLEET_FAMILY_CAP = claude=3, fable=1, ollama=5. claude=3: unchanged from T651 §7c.33, REINFORCED — the 2026-08-24 provider-429 came at only 4 runs in a 5-hour window, so 3 is the largest number that has not tripped the provider; the 2026-08-22 five-lane window death (12:47Z) would have been structurally impossible at 3. fable=1: unchanged (RESERVED appetite, shares the claude provider window). ollama=5: NEW — the provider's own recorded five-worker ceiling; the 2026-08-24 incident ran 7 ollama lanes only because the explicit door had no cap. deepseek/local: NO default cap — neither has a recorded provider ceiling, and inventing one is exactly the C5 constant-invention sin this task names; bounded by the total.
PENDING OPERATOR RATIFICATION: the code implements the proposal (default 4 / ollama=5). Rejection is a one-line change in tools/fleet_caps.py's two DEFAULT_* constants; the findings record makes the proposal auditable. This is the brief's own requested deliverable ("propose a total cap and per-family caps and defend each number"), not a silent overturn of the 2026-08-19 ruling.

== THE KEEPER COUNTER BUG FIXED ONCE (brief §2's "if the keeper's counter is wrong, fix it once, not twice") ==
The keeper's family_of split the model label on ':' BEFORE the map lookup, so its own "qwen3.8:27b-mlx": "local" entry was unreachable — every local lane counted as "other": uncapped AND appetite-SPEND, against the keeper's own local=PROBE intent (it would auto-dispatch a local qwen lane the design says must never auto-launch). Fixed in the shared helper: full label first, then the ':'-split prefix. Verified on the LIVE store: qwen3.8:27b-mlx now counts as family 'local'.

== THE FIVE CONTROLS (tools/regression-dispatch-caps.sh) — all RED against the pre-T845 bin/dispatch before GREEN, all PASS ==
1. cap-2 fixture: FLEET_CAP=2 with two rows in_progress → third dispatch refused naming "total cap: 2/2" + both waiting tasks; nothing spawned; one row leaves in_progress (reopen) → third succeeds. RED before (rc=0, no gate).
2. per-family: FLEET_FAMILY_CAP=claude=1 with a claude row running → second claude refused naming "family claude is at its cap: 1/1" + the waiter; a deepseek dispatch allowed. RED before.
3. override: at cap without override → refused; --override-cap=<reason> in dry-run → bypasses + warns + NOT recorded (a dry-run is not a decision); empty and bare --override-cap → refused 'requires a reason'; REAL dispatch with override → data line + reason recorded to the scratch ledger. RED before (the flag fell through to the unknown-flag usage refusal).
4. null: zero in_progress → dispatch behaves exactly as today (dry-run data line, no REFUSED). GREEN before and after (the null control's whole point).
5. keeper unchanged: same fixture → keeper --once logs 'at cap (2/2) — no dispatch' and prints 'cap'; family arm logs 'family-cap: T8711 family claude at cap 1/1' and dispatches the deepseek lane — the exact pre-T845 log format, with the count now coming from the shared helper. 5b doubles as the shared-counter proof: bin/dispatch's refusal says 2/2 and the keeper's log says (2/2) for the same fixture.
Plus a sixth control for brief §5 (the one-writer doctrine, which has no dedicated control in the brief): held file refused naming file + holder; a different file allowed; --override-cap does NOT bypass. And the closing telemetry-isolation scan (T512 shape): the suite's fixture ids (T870x) never reach the live heal log or perf ledger.

My own regression's fixture accumulation: arms left rows in_progress, so later arms' keeper fixtures carried stale in_progress rows and the cap messages reported accumulated counts (3/1 instead of 1/1).
